analysis: Reviewed the head-text excerpts of docs/architecture/inference.md (lines 4065-4922) and the patch excerpt. The only changed line is 2126, in the request-parameter table: the `stop` row now documents per-request ReasoningStopScope for Gemma 4 and <think> parsers, and says the native block engine carries no scope. This is documentation only and changes no code or security controls. The excerpts I was given (4065-4922) are unchanged context and contain no edits. They cover cluster GLM chunking, authenticated-record bounds, KV precision, SSD prefix record encoding, GPT-OSS/MiMo/Nemotron batch paths, and manifest pinning. They describe fail-closed load agreement, authenticated records, bounded sizes, and non-qualification claims. I found no claim that weakens T-041 mitigations (HMAC-keyed names, AES-GCM, TTL, salt scoping). The cluster SSD prefix record text says the encoding is sealed in the header and in the directory name, and records of another encoding are refused and deleted, consistent with the existing cache threat posture. The changed stop-scope row at line 2126 is outside the supplied units, so I could not examine it in context. Remaining integration question: the actual code in EngineV2Bridge+StopSequence.swift and ReasoningStopScope is not supplied, so I cannot verify that the docs match the implementation or that stop-sequence matching cannot leak or truncate reasoning or tool-call content. That is an integrity and behavior question, not a demonstrated security regression. No new attack surface or invalidated threat-model assumptions are evident from the supplied documentation.
